items.title: Add agent performance metrics and OTEL observability stack
items.body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive agent performance measurement and observability tooling to Claude Code. Introduces two complementary systems: a transcript-based metrics parser for daily use and historical tracking, and an optional OTEL + Grafana stack for live dashboards and real-dollar cost attribution.

## Key Changes

**Agent metrics tool** (`.claude/tools/agent-metrics.py`):
- Parses Claude Code's own JSONL session transcripts to extract per-agent performance data
- Reports: turns (agentic loop length), tool calls, output tokens, context window usage, cache re-read overhead, and wall-clock duration
- Aggregates by agent type and supports filtering by session
- Outputs human-readable tables or machine-readable JSON for trend tracking
- No telemetry setup required; reads existing transcript files

**Durable metrics log** (`.claude/metrics/agent-runs.jsonl`):
- `SubagentStop` and `Stop` hooks (via `.claude/hooks/capture-agent-metrics.sh`) automatically sync finished runs into a persistent log
- Survives Claude Code's ~30-day transcript pruning
- Idempotent and self-healing (mid-flight runs overwritten by final numbers on next sync)
- Enables long-term performance trend tracking

**OTEL observability stack** (`.claude/otel/`):
- Docker Compose setup: OpenTelemetry Collector + Prometheus + Grafana
- Pre-built dashboard (`claude-agents.json`) showing cost per agent, tokens per agent, cost breakdown, and time-series trends
- `telemetry.env` and `telemetry-off.sh` for per-terminal opt-in
- Comprehensive `OTEL-ReadMe.md` explaining the stack and how to interpret the charts

**Documentation**:
- `.claude/tools/README.md`: Method for diagnosing slowdowns (SOT vs agents vs code), establishing baselines, and scaling strategies
- Explains `maxTurns` guardrail and how to set it from measured data
- Guidance on making agent communication reliable

**Agent safety guardrails**:
- Added `maxTurns: 80` to all forge agents (code-writer, code-cleaner, code-reviewer, doc-planner, doc-writer, prd-author, prd-reviewer, prd-alignment, test-author, test-auditor)
- Caps agentic loop length to fail fast on runaway agents

**Configuration**:
- Updated `.claude/settings.json` to wire the metrics capture hook to `SubagentStop` and `Stop` events
- Added `.gitignore` files to exclude metrics logs and Python cache

## Notable Implementation Details

- Agent type discovery mines the parent session transcripts by matching `Agent`/`Task` tool uses with their result payloads (which embed `agentId`)
- Context window calculation: `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` — shows the true cost of re-reading on each dispatch
- Metrics are keyed by `agentId` (the run's unique identifier), not agent name, so the same agent type can be tracked across multiple runs
- OTEL metrics use `query_source="subagent"` label to distinguish agent work from main loop, enabling per-agent cost attribution in Grafana
- Both tools are system-agnostic (not gated on active system) so they work under any agent framework

items.title: Handle `-%` LeetPush metrics in README update workflow
items.body:
The `update-readme` Actions job failed in `Run LeetCode script` when commit messages contained placeholder performance metrics (`-%`) instead of numeric percentages. The parser in `.github/workflows/script.sh` treated this as a hard failure under `set -e`.

- **Root cause**
  - Metric extraction only matched numeric values (`[0-9.]+%`), so `grep` failed on `-%` and terminated the script early.

- **Script parsing hardening**
  - Updated metric regexes to accept both numeric and placeholder formats:
    - `Time Beats: (-|[0-9.]+)%`
    - `Memory Beats: (-|[0-9.]+)%`
  - Added non-fatal extraction behavior (`|| true`) so parse misses flow into existing validation logic instead of immediate shell exit.

- **Behavioral impact**
  - Commits like `[Time Beats: -%] [Memory Beats: -%]` are now handled as valid input for README generation.
  - Truly missing/invalid metrics still fail via the explicit validation guard.

```bash
TIME_BEATS=$(echo "$RAW_COMMIT" \
  | grep -oE 'Time Beats: (-|[0-9.]+)%' \
  | grep -oE '(-|[0-9.]+)%' || true)

MEMORY_BEATS=$(echo "$RAW_COMMIT" \
  | grep -oE 'Memory Beats: (-|[0-9.]+)%' \
  | grep -oE '(-|[0-9.]+)%' || true)
```

## What

Adds `doc/cli-performance-metrics.md`, a developer doc for the CLI performance-metrics
pipeline that `pulumi-trace-tool` powers: how `pulumi --tracing` output flows through the
`tocsv` and `metrics` subcommands, what each metric means, and where the CI benchmarks that
feed it live.

## Why

The doc previously lived apart from the code it describes. It references this repo's
`traces/metric_names.go` and the `tocsv` / `metrics` subcommands directly, so keeping it next
to that code is the natural home and keeps the two from drifting. The repo had no docs area,
so this adds a `doc/` directory.

## Accuracy

Every command, flag, metric name, and code link in the doc was verified against the current
source:

- Metric names and descriptions match `traces/metric_names.go` and `traces/metrics.go` — e.g.
  the total-wall-time metric is `time_total_ms`, and `time_pulumi_api_ms` is an interval union
  (overlapping requests counted once, not summed). The engine-span metrics (`time_engine_ms` /

items.body:
The ResoTrade 24-month backtest (+26.1% vs HODL) was a private, non-reproducible implementation (deficiency M-5). This adds a fully public walk-forward backtest module built directly on the existing `resonance_logic_example.py` logic.

## New: `backtest/backtest_engine.py` (EN + DE mirror)

- **`fetch_btcusdt_ohlcv()`** — data loading with priority chain: Binance Public API → ccxt → deterministic synthetic fallback (`seed=42`, DC `30_000 + 0.5t + 2000·sin(2πt/800)`, AC cycles 50h/120h/20h, noise σ=150 USDT). API limit warning when `n_candles > 1000`.
- **`walk_forward_split()`** — strict temporal split into N folds, zero train/test overlap, no look-ahead bias, `fold_id` tracked throughout.
- **`ResoTradeBacktest`** — experience-store pre-training on train fold, evaluation on test fold, trade log export (CSV with UTC header), and `performance_metrics()` returning explicit falsification verdict:

```python

# metrics['m5_closed']     → bool
```

items.title: Add Study 1 perturbability model
items.body:
## What changed

- Added `scripts/07a_build_perturbability_model.R` to convert the hardened Q3 finding into a portable Study 1 ecological perturbability model.
- Uses one target per independent cow-quarter trajectory: mean Bray-Curtis displacement across T2/T3 from that quarter's T1 baseline.
- Prespecifies four transportable baseline predictors: richness, Shannon diversity, evenness, and dominance.
- Uses ridge regularization because these ecological predictors are correlated and the discovery cohort contains only 20 trajectories.
- Estimates discovery performance with nested leave-one-cow-out validation so all quarters from the held-out cow remain out of training and hyperparameter tuning.
- Adds 5,000-replicate cow-level bootstrap uncertainty by default.
- Added `scripts/07b_apply_perturbability_model.R` for outcome-blind external prediction.
- Added `docs/perturbability_model_v1.md` with the frozen Manitoba validation protocol and interpretation boundaries.
- Updated README to distinguish Q3 association, perturbability prediction, external validation, and the later mastitis-risk hypothesis.

## Why

The current Q3 analysis demonstrates that baseline ecological state is associated with future displacement. This change formalizes that result as a falsifiable prediction model suitable for external validation rather than treating the discovery coefficients as a clinical score.

## Validation design

Internal performance is nested cow-blocked cross-validation. External validation is explicitly outcome-blind: baseline Manitoba predictions are generated and frozen before observed follow-up displacement is calculated or inspected. Spearman rank transportability is designated as the primary external endpoint because the validation cohort uses a different 16S region/protocol.

## Important limitation

The GitHub environment does not contain the workstation's production Q3 result table, so the model architecture is implemented but coefficients and performance metrics are intentionally not fabricated. The next step is to run `MMER_BOOTSTRAPS=5000 Rscript scripts/07a_build_perturbability_model.R` on the production workstation and archive the resulting frozen model outputs.

## Summary

- make the project-facing language hardware-neutral while retaining H20 as the exact recorded measurement target
- pin the comparison baseline to FlashInfer 0.6.17
- publish a current-source BF16 eager-provider attention benchmark with all raw samples
- add a concise website/README comparison that shows both strengths and known gaps

## Performance result

The accepted run covers 14 matched attention shapes in both provider orders, with 200 warmups and 100 combined samples per provider/shape (2,800 latency samples total).

- 14/14 shapes have provider-order median drift at or below 5% for both providers
- Oxide Infer has lower combined median latency in 8 shapes
- FlashInfer has lower combined median latency in 6 shapes
- the largest measured gap is long paged-prefill GQA4: 265.66 µs vs 23.08 µs, or 11.51× lower latency for FlashInfer

These are eager-provider CUDA-event microbenchmarks on the recorded NVIDIA H20. They are not isolated-kernel, CUDA Graph, model, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, memory, or serving claims, and the PR makes no overall-winner claim.

No Rust product source files change in this PR. The implementation source remains the merged `7f3d08e` tree; this change publishes the R2 baseline, comparison tooling pin, documentation, and website presentation.

# 🚀 Performance Optimization and Production Build

## 📋 Overview

This PR implements comprehensive performance optimizations for the Cryptocurrency Dashboard Landing Page, preparing it for production deployment on GitHub Pages. The changes focus on reducing bundle size, implementing code splitting, lazy loading strategies, and ensuring optimal Core Web Vitals metrics.

## ✨ What's Implemented

### Performance Optimizations
- ⚡ **Code Splitting**: Implemented React.lazy() for non-critical components (MarketTrendTable, QuickTransferPreview, Footer)
- 🖼️ **Image Optimization**: Added lazy loading for below-the-fold images with proper sizing parameters
- 📦 **Bundle Optimization**: Configured Vite for optimal chunk splitting and vendor code separation
- 🛡️ **Error Handling**: Added ErrorBoundary component for graceful failure handling
- 🌐 **API Resilience**: Implemented timeout and retry logic for CoinGecko API calls
- 🎯 **Resource Hints**: Added dns-prefetch and preconnect meta tags for external resources

### Production Build Configuration
- ✅ Optimized Vite build settings with aggressive minification
- ✅ Configured proper base path for GitHub Pages deployment
- ✅ Implemented manual chunk splitting for vendor dependencies
- ✅ Disabled source maps for production builds
- ✅ Enhanced CSS code splitting

## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria Status

| Criteria | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Production build completes successfully | ✅ | Optimized bundles generated |
| Main bundle size <200KB gzipped | ✅ | Achieved through code splitting |
| Lighthouse Performance >90 (desktop), >80 (mobile) | ⏳ | To be verified post-deployment |
| First Contentful Paint (FCP) <1.5s on 3G | ⏳ | To be verified post-deployment |
| Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) <2.5s | ⏳ | To be verified post-deployment |
| Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) <0.1 | ✅ | Explicit image dimensions added |

| Build output includes cache headers & hashing | ✅ | Vite handles automatically |
| GitHub Pages deployment configured | ✅ | Base path properly set |
| API calls have error handling & timeouts | ✅ | 5s timeout with retry logic |

## 🔧 Technical Approach

### Code Splitting Strategy
```javascript
// Lazy-loaded components with Suspense fallbacks
const MarketTrendTable = lazy(() => import('./components/MarketTrendTable.jsx'));
const QuickTransferPreview = lazy(() => import('./components/QuickTransferPreview.jsx'));
const Footer = lazy(() => import('./components/Footer.jsx'));
```

### Error Boundary Implementation
- Created `ErrorBoundary` component to catch and handle errors from lazy-loaded components
- Provides user-friendly fallback UI with reload option
- Logs errors for debugging purposes

### API Optimization
- Implemented `AbortController` with 5-second timeout
- Added exponential backoff retry logic (max 2 retries)
- Enhanced error messages for different failure scenarios

### Build Configuration
- **Vendor Chunking**: Separated React/React-DOM into dedicated vendor bundle
- **Minification**: Terser with aggressive optimization settings
- **Asset Inlining**: Small assets (<4KB) inlined as base64
- **CSS Splitting**: Enabled for better caching

## 📁 Files Changed

### Modified Files
- **`src/App.jsx`** - Implemented lazy loading for 3 components with Suspense wrappers
- **`vite.config.js`** - Optimized build configuration for production
- **`index.html`** - Added performance meta tags and resource hints
- **`src/components/CryptoCarousel.jsx`** - Enhanced API error handling with timeout
- **`src/components/HeroSection.jsx`** - Added lazy loading to background image

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```
- Verify all components load correctly
- Check that lazy-loaded components appear with loading states
- Test error boundary by simulating component errors

### 2. Production Build Test

```bash
npm run build
```

## What

Removes the two telemetry/data-collection systems from FCM, keeping **Device Keypair Auth** (which is security/auth, not telemetry):

- **Client Performance Metrics** — `/client-performance` page, `client_metrics` table, `clientMetricsService`, `POST /api/client-metrics` ingest + admin/debug routes, the daily purge job.

Motivation: privacy (explicit no-telemetry stance) **and** simplification. Spec + plan are on the branch under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Key changes

- **Backend:** deleted `telemetryService`, `clientMetricsService`, `adminTelemetry`, `clientMetricsPurge`; `POST /api/client-metrics` is now a **`410 Gone` tombstone**; the WS connect handler emits a hardcoded **`telemetry:set { enabled: false }` kill-switch** (no DB lookup); `broadcastTelemetrySet` removed; **`versionDistribution` dropped** from `community-stats` (its only source, `client_metrics`, is gone — no alternative source).
- **DB:** removed the `TelemetrySetting` + `ClientMetric` models; idempotent migration `20260618000000_drop_telemetry_and_client_metrics` (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS … CASCADE`). **This purges all collected rows at deploy.**
- **Dashboard:** removed the `/telemetry` and `/client-performance` pages, routes, and SYSTEM-tab nav entries; deleted `Telemetry.tsx` + the `client-performance/` folder. `/devices` and `/server-health` kept.
- **Docs:** updated architecture / backend (api-reference, services, jobs) / database / realtime / frontend docs; re-documented `telemetry:set` as a deprecated always-`false` kill-switch (not deleted); added a **no-telemetry privacy statement** to `README.md` and `docs/overlay/README.md`.

## Privacy goal is achieved at server deploy

The desktop client never shipped any telemetry emit code (verified — no sender, no `telemetry:set` handler, no monitor process), so **no overlay release is needed**. Once the server deploys, the `410` endpoint stores nothing and the kill-switch tells any out-of-repo client to stop. The `410` + kill-switch are belt-and-suspenders for already-installed clients.

## Blast radius — no other service affected

Three external touch-points, all handled: the WS connect handler (kill-switch), `communityStatsService` (field dropped), dashboard nav/routes. Shared infra (`requireClientAuth`, `requireDiscordRole`, `requireAdminKey`, Redis, logger, job-tracker) untouched; Device Keypair Auth untouched; no Discord-bot/public-website consumers; tables have no foreign keys.

## Testing

- New backend tests: `clientMetricsRemoved` (410 + admin 404), `communityStatsNoVersionDist` (shape omits the field, siblings intact), `telemetryRemoved` (route 404 + real `handleConnection()` kill-switch test, proven via negative control). **All pass.**

- The full local `npm test` can't run without Postgres/Redis (unrelated branch-untouched suites fail on `DATABASE_URL`) — **CI is the authoritative gate** (provisions DB/Redis).

## After merge

Promoting `dev → prod` is a separate, deliberate step (merge commit): it triggers a real prod deploy that **drops the tables** and activates the `410`/kill-switch.

items.title: harden sealed holdout cutoff and warm-up
items.body:
## What changed

- pass the exact timezone-aware `as_of` cutoff through RAW -> DDS
- collect a fixed 208-bar pre-holdout warm-up on a fresh database so EMA-200 and its 10-value slope exist at the first holdout candle
- separate event-time replay cutoff from RAW ingestion progression inside `dds.load_raw_candles(...)`
- add regression coverage for fresh-database warm-up, DDS cutoff propagation, and RAW rows whose `loaded_at > as_of` while `close_time <= as_of`
- update README, STATUS and ROADMAP to reflect the sealed validation phase and the paper/live blockers

## Root cause

The incremental updater originally used one cutoff for collection, derived calculations and health, while RAW -> DDS used wall-clock time. PR #35 initially changed RAW -> DDS to pass the replay `as_of`, but review found that `dds.load_raw_candles(...)` also used `p_as_of` as a `loaded_at` cutoff. Because collection happens after `as_of` is fixed, newly inserted RAW rows can legitimately have `loaded_at > as_of` even though their candle `close_time <= as_of`.

The corrected contract separates the two time axes:

- `p_as_of` is the causal/event-time cutoff (`close_time <= p_as_of`)
- RAW ingestion progression is bounded independently by a DB `clock_timestamp()` captured at function start

This allows historical replay to ingest RAW that was written after the replay timestamp without allowing open/future candles through the event-time cutoff.

When no collector checkpoint exists, collection starts 208 completed 1h bars before the holdout boundary to provide EMA-200 plus the required 10-value EMA-200 slope history.

## Safety

The holdout remains performance-sealed until `2027-02-06T00:00:00Z`. These changes do not import or execute the strategy, do not compute performance metrics and do not enable paper or live trading.

## Validation
